title: Model Routing & Cost-Aware Fallbacks (PRD + Roadmap + Pricing)
author: Maya Thompson
summary:
This consolidated product document defines the PRD, design specifications, roadmap, and pricing/packaging considerations for Model Routing & Cost-Aware Fallbacks

 a platform capability to route inference requests across model variants and deployment tiers to meet customer latency, cost, and reliability objectives.
overview:
Problem: Customers running at scale want predictable latency and lower unit cost while preserving output quality. When capacity or price constraints occur, applications must gracefully degrade without engineering complex client-side logic.

Solution: Provide a server-side, policy-driven model routing layer that: 1) routes requests by latency/cost/quality policies, 2) implements transparent fallbacks to compatible model variants or alternate capacity tiers, and 3) exposes cost and quality tradeoffs in the Console and API. This feature complements Redwood Optimize and the runtime's smart routing capabilities.
product_goals:
1) Reduce average per-token cost for customers with mixed workloads by 10-25% via policy-driven routing and automatic fallbacks.
2) Ensure 99.9% availability for routed requests with automatic fallback paths.
3) Make routing policies easy to configure via Console and API templates and provide observability that makes cost/quality tradeoffs auditable.
4) Ship an MVP that supports hosted and Dedicated deployments in H2 2026; Private deployment support planned for early 2027.
success_metrics:
- Cost reduction: mean per-token spend decreased by >=10% for participating customers within 30 days of enabling.
- Reliability: routed requests maintain 99.9% successful response rate with fallback used at most 5% of the time for normal operations.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile routing decision latency < 25ms.
- Adoption: >=20 paying customers enable routing policies in first quarter after GA.
non_goals:
- This work will not include training or fine-tuning models.
- The MVP will not include automated quality-based model retraining.
- Immediate support for arbitrary third-party endpoints (external model providers) is deferred to a future phase.
requirements:
Mandatory requirements (MUST):

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Policy DSL for routing | Console + API allow users to define routing policies by: latency SLA, max cost-per-token, model family whitelist, and region preference. Test: create policy and show traffic routed accordingly. | Product/Backend |
| R2 | Fallback graph & compatibility registry | System stores model compatibility metadata (input tokenization, sequence length limits, output format) so runtime can select compatible fallback. Test: runtime falls back without payload transformation required. | Runtime/Model-Onboarding |
| R3 | Observability & audit trail | Per-request routing decision logged (policy ID, selected path, reason). Console exposes per-policy cost & quality impact. | Observability Team |
| R4 | Graceful degradation | On capacity constraint or degraded latency, requests follow fallback graph automatically within policy constraints. Test: induced capacity drop triggers allowed fallback and response served. | Serving Runtime |
| R5 | Backwards-compatible API | No breaking changes to existing generation/chat APIs; routing is opt-in via policyId parameter. | API/SDKs |

Optional / Nice-to-have (SHOULD):
- Weighted A/B routing for gradual rollouts.
- Client-side SDK helpers for policy preview.
- Integration with Redwood Optimize recommendations for auto-generated policies.
design_spec:
High-level design:

1) Components:
- Policy Service (config store + DSL parser): stores user policies, validates constraints, and exposes an API for policy evaluation.
- Compatibility Registry: metadata about models and variants (input/output constraints, quantization compatibility, throughput profiles).
- Routing Decision Engine (low-latency): evaluates policy, current capacity/latency signals, and model compatibility to return target model/variant.
- Fallback Executor (runtime integration): instructs serving runtime to select alternate model/variant or alternate capacity tier (e.g., Dedicated -> Hosted) and manages KV cache consistency where needed.
- Observability Pipeline: structured logs + metrics for every routing decision (policyId, decisionTimeMs, selectedModel, fallbacksAttempted, costEstimate).

2) Policy DSL example:
policy {
  id: "cost-aware-low-latency"
  constraints {
    max_cost_per_token: 0.0008
    latency_sla_ms: 200
    allowed_models: ["redwood-2-small", "redwood-2-medium", "redwood-2-large-quantized"]
    fallback_preference: ["same-region", "lower-cost-variant", "different-tier"]
  }
  actions {
    prefer_cache: true
    allow_partial_response: false
  }
}

3) Decision flow (runtime):
- Receive request with policyId (or account default).
- Query Policy Service for constraints.
- Query capacity & latency signals (Realtime metrics store).
- Consult Compatibility Registry for candidate models.
- Evaluate candidates against policy constraints and select one; if none meet constraints, use fallback chain as defined.
- Emit routing decision event and invoke serving runtime with selected model variant.

4) Performance considerations:
- Routing Decision Engine must be <25ms median and <50ms 95p in 95% of calls. Use cached policy evaluations and precomputed candidate lists per region.
- Compatibility metadata kept in a small in-memory store refreshed every minute.

5) Security & multi-tenancy:
- Policies are scoped to account/org. RBAC ensures only org admins can change routing policies. Audit logs stored for 1 year for enterprise customers (configurable retention).
api_and_console_changes:
API:
- New optional parameter on generation/chat endpoints: policy_id (string).
- New endpoints: POST /v1/policies (create), GET /v1/policies/{id}, PATCH /v1/policies/{id}, DELETE /v1/policies/{id}.
- Policies are versioned; create returns policy_id and revision.

Console:
- New Policies page under Model management.
- Quickstart templates: Cost-aware low-latency, Cost-priority, Low-cost-batch.
- Per-policy dashboard: traffic split, cost delta vs baseline, fallback rate, error/fallback reasons.

SDKs:
- Simple wrapper to pass policy_id and to preview routing decision given a sample payload.
roadmap_and_timeline:
Q2 2026 (Discovery & Spec): finalize DSL and compatibility metadata schema; prototype Decision Engine with synthetic signals.
Q3 2026 (MVP): implement Policy Service, Compatibility Registry, basic Decision Engine, Console policy UI, and API endpoints. Limited beta with 5-8 customers (hosted + Dedicated).
Q4 2026 (GA): performance hardening, observability dashboards, pricing integration, Private deployment support planning.
H1 2027: Private deployment GA and advanced features (A/B weighted routing, auto-policy suggestions from Redwood Optimize).

Milestones & owners:
- Policy DSL finalization (Product) - 2026-04-15

- Beta release (Eng + SRE) - 2026-08-15
- GA (Cross-functional) - 2026-11-01
pricing_and_packaging_notes:
Pricing principles:
- Routing and fallbacks are primarily a control-plane feature; customers should not be charged per-decision.
- Billing model will reflect the execution costs: customers pay for tokens generated by the selected model variant and for any Dedicated capacity consumed.
- Add-on: Advanced routing analytics (longer retention, custom alerts) available as a paid add-on for enterprise.

Proposed packaging:
- Included in Hosted API & Dedicated by default for customers on Standard and Enterprise plans.
- For Dedicated customers, routing across Dedicated pools vs Hosted bursts will be controlled by config and incurs standard Dedicated vs Hosted billing rates.
- Enterprise-only features: 1-year audit retention, custom policy SLA, and priority rollout assistance.

Estimated revenue impact:
- Enablement expected to increase Dedicated commit sizes (customers prefer deterministic fallbacks); conservative estimate +5-8% ARR expansion for mid-sized customers using advanced policies.

Monitoring billing edge-cases:
- Ensure clear invoices: record which model served each request (model_id) and tier (hosted/dedicated) in billing metadata.
rollout_plan_and_risks:
Rollout steps (beta -> GA):
1) Internal dogfood: enable on Redwood Console for non-production accounts and run synthetic traffic.
2) Early beta with select accounts: define 2-3 canonical policies per customer and monitor fallback rates and cost deltas for 30 days.
3) Expand beta (20 customers) with automated observability alerts.
4) GA with documentation, SDK examples, and recommended templates.

Key risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Incorrect compatibility metadata causes runtime errors. Mitigation: strict validation in model onboarding and unit tests; fall back to safe model and emit high-severity alert.
- Risk: Unexpected cost spikes from misconfigured policies. Mitigation: default safe limits (max_cost_per_token) enforced at creation and a mandatory preview that estimates cost impact.
- Risk: Increased decision latency. Mitigation: caching, precomputed candidate lists, and a fast-path with conservative defaults.
- Risk: Data residency concerns for Private deployments. Mitigation: local policy service and compatibility registry packaged for on-prem with KMS integration.

qa_and_validation:
Test plan highlights:
1) Unit & integration tests for DSL parsing and policy versioning.
2) End-to-end test harness that injects synthetic capacity and latency signals to validate fallback behavior.
3) Load tests to verify decision engine latency at 10k req/s scale.
4) Billing reconciliation tests to ensure accurate model/tier attribution.
5) Security review and threat model for cross-tenant policy isolation.
